# Requirement #2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.

**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

requirement_points.text: Building the repro `app` project, where `Cmd` has a member of type `Item<int>` and `Item<T>` is a `record struct` or plain `struct` declared in the referenced `lib` assembly, completes without the generator emitting CS8785.
The same build completes without the analyzer emitting AD0001.
The build output for `app` contains a generated `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` type, so the generator contributes source to the compilation.
The generated resolver for `app` includes a formatter for `Cmd` and a formatter for `Item<int>` (or its open generic definition) so that the member is covered.

plants.description: Reintroduces direct indexing of DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] for a property symbol. When the property comes from metadata (e.g., the Key property of Item<int> from the referenced lib assembly), the collection is empty and the generator throws IndexOutOfRangeException, producing CS8785 and no generated resolver.

Reintroduces direct indexing of DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] for a field symbol. When the field comes from metadata, the collection is empty and the generator throws IndexOutOfRangeException, preventing the resolver from being generated.

Removes the IsInSource guard before calling ContainsSyntaxTree. For diagnostics whose location is not in source (metadata symbols), Location.SourceTree is null and ContainsSyntaxTree throws ArgumentNullException, which surfaces as AD0001 in the analyzer.

Bypasses the ReportIfLocatedInCompilation filter entirely. The analyzer will report diagnostics for symbols from referenced assemblies, which can have locations outside the compilation and cause AD0001.
Removes the null-conditional operator on reportDiagnostic. In the source generator context reportDiagnostic is null, so invoking this diagnostic path throws NullReferenceException, producing CS8785.

Removes the null-conditional operator after FirstOrDefault(). For metadata symbols FirstOrDefault() returns null, so calling GetSyntax() throws NullReferenceException, crashing the generator and preventing the resolver from being emitted.

Omits the ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper so diagnostics for metadata symbols are reported directly. Analyzers are not permitted to report against locations outside the compilation, which causes AD0001.
Uses a named argument when calling GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. No behavioural change.
Adds a redundant null-conditional operator after GetSyntax(). GetSyntax() never returns null, so behaviour is unchanged.
Adds a null-forgiving operator to SourceTree. The preceding IsInSource check already guarantees it is non-null, so behaviour is unchanged.

points.reason: The GetObjectInfo diagnostic paths that indexed DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly are replaced with FirstOrDefault-based location helpers (GetPropertyIdentifierLocation and FirstOrDefault()?.), so a closed generic value type from metadata no longer throws IndexOutOfRangeException and CS8785 is not raised; the test asserts zero generator warnings.

reportDiagnostic now routes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which drops diagnostics whose location is not in the compilation being analyzed, so metadata-defined types' member diagnostics are not reported by the consuming project and AD0001 is not raised; the analyzer test run fails on any diagnostic.
The generator runs to completion and contributes source; the test asserts the expected resolver hint name is present among the generated sources.
With the crash fixed, the generator emits the complete resolver including formatters for Cmd and its Item<int> member type; the test confirms the resolver is produced without warnings.

findings.message: DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] is accessed directly without checking if the collection is empty. For metadata symbols from referenced assemblies this collection is empty and the access throws IndexOutOfRangeException, the same defect class as the reported issue. The reportDiagnostic wrapper at line 239 does not prevent it because the [0] access occurs during Diagnostic.Create before the wrapper is invoked.

points.reason: The reportDiagnostic wrapper filters diagnostics to the compilation being analyzed, and FirstOrDefault() replaces unsafe [0] access at line 1077, preventing the generator crash (CS8785) for the reported repro.
Same changes prevent the analyzer from throwing AD0001 when processing closed generic value types from referenced assemblies.
RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync asserts the expected resolver hint name is present in generated sources, confirming the generator contributes output to the usage assembly.
With the generator no longer crashing, the generated resolver for the usage assembly includes formatters for all members, including the closed generic value type member.

findings.message: MemberNeedsKey diagnostic still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly, which throws IndexOutOfRangeException for metadata symbols. This edge case (a metadata type member lacking a key) is not covered by the fix and could still crash the generator or analyzer.

points.reason: The reportDiagnostic callback is wrapped to drop diagnostics from metadata (line 239), and the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic location now uses the safe GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper (line 985, defined at 1434) instead of indexing DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] directly, preventing the generator crash for the repro scenario.

The ReportIfLocatedInCompilation wrapper (lines 1444-1450) filters out diagnostics whose location is not in the source trees of the compilation being analyzed, so the analyzer no longer reports AD0001 for members of types defined in referenced assemblies.

The test RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync runs the generator directly and asserts that the expected resolver hint name is present in the generated sources (line 658), confirming the generator contributes output.

With the generator no longer crashing, it runs to completion and emits the resolver; the resolver generation logic (unchanged by this PR) includes formatters for Cmd and its Item<int> member as it would for any in-source type.

ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference reproduces the exact issue (record struct Item<T> in referenced assembly, used by Cmd in the consuming project), and RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync asserts no warnings, which covers CS8785 from the generator. Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.

The same test and helper assert no diagnostics at Warning severity or higher, which covers AD0001 from the analyzer, since both use the same TypeCollector code paths. Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.
RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync asserts the expected resolver hint name is present in runResult.Results generated sources, proving the generator contributed output.

The generator successfully processes Cmd, which has an Item<int> member, and emits the resolver without crashing; generating a resolver for Cmd requires covering the Item<int> member with a formatter. Its citations were too broad to count as evidence.

Replaces direct DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] indexing with FirstOrDefault() patterns at diagnostic emission sites inside GetObjectInfo, preventing IndexOutOfRangeException when the type is a closed generic value type from a metadata reference with no syntax.
The analyzer shares the same TypeCollector code path; the same FirstOrDefault() guards prevent the analyzer from crashing on metadata symbols.
By preventing the generator crash, the generator can now complete and contribute the GeneratedMessagePackResolver source to the compilation instead of silently emitting none.

The fix allows the generator to run to completion for the exact repro scenario (record struct Item<T> from a referenced assembly used as a Cmd member), and the added test verifies the resolver is generated, which includes formatters for Cmd and Item<int>.

findings.message: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation dereferences diagnostic.Location.IsInSource without a null check. When a diagnostic is created with a null location (for example from GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returning null for a metadata symbol, or from the FirstOrDefault() change at line 1077), this throws NullReferenceException. The analyzer or generator would still fail instead of producing a clean build, just with a different exception than the original IndexOutOfRangeException.

Changes this.reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(...) to this.reportDiagnostic.Invoke(...). If reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null (valid per the nullable constructor parameter), reportDiagnostic is null and this throws NullReferenceException. The original code was null-safe with ?.Invoke.

Whether the NullReferenceException at line 1446 is triggered for the specific repro scenario, since it depends on whether diagnostics with null locations are created for metadata properties during execution of the repro.

For a member symbol from metadata (empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences), FirstOrDefault() returns null and .GetSyntax() throws NullReferenceException, so the generator/analyzer still crashes on closed generic value types from referenced assemblies that have members without a key (e.g. the added ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember test). # Requirement #2283: Generator and analyzer must report MsgPack004 for unkeyed members of closed generic structs from referenced assemblies

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**. In addition, when that referenced generic value type has a public member without a `Key` attribute, the analyzer must report `MsgPack004` in the consuming assembly, using the location of the member usage in the consuming assembly. Today the crash prevents any diagnostic, and even when the crash is avoided the unkeyed member is silently ignored, so the consuming project gets no warning. Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key)
{
    public int Unkeyed { get; init; }
}
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`, and a `MsgPack004` diagnostic reported in `app` for `Item<int>.Unkeyed` at the member usage in `Cmd`. The diagnostic must not be suppressed just because `Item<T>` is declared in a referenced assembly.

#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`, and no `MsgPack004` is reported for `Item<int>.Unkeyed`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols. The `MsgPack004` requirement applies whenever the referenced generic value type has an unkeyed public member.

**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter and losing the required `MsgPack004` diagnostic.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

findings.message: reportDiagnostic is wrapped in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, which drops diagnostics for members from referenced assemblies instead of reporting MsgPack004 in the consuming assembly as the requirement demands.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation suppresses any diagnostic whose location is not in the current compilation, so an unkeyed public member of a referenced generic value type never produces MsgPack004 in the consuming project.

Test ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember asserts zero diagnostics for an unkeyed member from a referenced assembly, directly contradicting the requirement that MsgPack004 must be reported in the consuming assembly.
